title: North Sikkim package costs explained
meta_description: What a North Sikkim 2N/3D or 3N/4D trip really costs in 2026: shared seat vs reserved SUV, lodge bands, Zero Point extra and what is included.
summary: A 2N/3D North Sikkim trip from Gangtok costs about ₹6,500–9,000 per person on a shared seat with a basic lodge, and about ₹11,000–14,000 each for a couple in a reserved SUV. A 3N/4D Lachen–Lachung loop runs ₹10,000–17,000 per person depending on group size. Figures are indicative for 2026.

sections.heading: The one number that sets the price
paras: The biggest line in any North Sikkim quote is not the hotel. It is the vehicle. Everything north of Mangan sits inside a Protected Area, so the trip must run in a registered North Sikkim SUV with a local driver, and that vehicle costs the same whether two people sit in it or six. Fill it and the price per person nearly halves.

That is why you see such different prices for what looks like the same trip. A couple in their own Scorpio and a solo traveller on a shared seat are buying the same road, the same permit and often the same lodge, but split the vehicle very differently.
All figures below are indicative 2026 ranges in INR, per person on twin sharing unless we say otherwise. Season, lodge and the state of the road move them. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Shared seat or reserved vehicle
paras: A shared seat means you buy a place in a Bolero, Sumo or Scorpio that leaves Gangtok for Lachung or Lachen with other travellers. The operator bundles the permit, a basic lodge and set meals. You move on a fixed timetable and the lodge is their choice. For solo travellers and young couples it is the cheapest honest way north.

A reserved vehicle is yours for the whole trip. You choose the lodge tier, stop where you like within the permit rules, and keep your luggage in one place. For families with elders, photographers and anyone travelling as four to six, it is usually the better buy.

sections.heading: What lodges cost in Lachung and Lachen
paras: North Sikkim lodges are simpler than Gangtok hotels at the same price. You arrive in the dark and leave at dawn for Yumthang or Gurudongmar, so most of the money goes on warmth and hot water rather than views. Rates almost always include dinner and breakfast, and many include lunch on the excursion day.

Indicative 2026 bands per room per night, with meals: budget ≈ ₹2,000–3,000, for a clean room, a shared heater and bucket hot water; standard ≈ ₹3,000–4,500, with an attached bathroom, a geyser and an electric blanket; premium ≈ ₹5,000–8,000, with a larger room and a room heater. Lachung has one or two resorts above ₹12,000 a night. Lachen has no luxury stock, and after the long closure some lodges are still reopening.
Homestays in Dzongu, if you add a night there, cost ≈ ₹1,500–2,500 per person with all meals.

sections.heading: Worked examples for 2026
paras: Here are the trips most people ask us for, priced from Gangtok and back. They leave out Gangtok hotels, the Bagdogra or NJP transfer, flights and 5 percent GST on package quotes.
list: 2N/3D Lachung, shared seat, budget lodge: seat with permit ≈ ₹3,000–3,500, two nights with meals ≈ ₹3,000–4,000 each. Total ≈ ₹6,500–8,000 per person.
2N/3D Lachung, couple, reserved Scorpio, standard lodge: vehicle ≈ ₹16,000 split two ways is ₹8,000 each, lodge ≈ ₹3,500 each for two nights, Zero Point ≈ ₹1,750 each. Total ≈ ₹13,000 per person.
3N/4D Lachen 2 nights and Lachung 1, couple, reserved Scorpio, standard lodges: vehicle ≈ ₹23,000 is ₹11,500 each, lodges ≈ ₹5,250 each. Total ≈ ₹16,500–17,500 per person with Zero Point.
The same 3N/4D loop for six friends in one Scorpio: vehicle ≈ ₹3,800 each, lodges ≈ ₹5,250 each. Total ≈ ₹9,500–10,000 per person.

sections.heading: What is included and what is not
paras: A fair North Sikkim package from Gangtok includes the vehicle with driver and fuel, the driver's stay and food, permit processing, lodges with dinner and breakfast, and usually lunch on the drive days. It should name the vehicle model and tell you whether the lodges are budget, standard or premium.

What is usually not included: the Zero Point extension of ≈ ₹3,000–4,000 per vehicle, paid in Lachung and dependent on snow; snow boots, coats and gloves hired at ≈ ₹100–300 an item; room heater charges at some lodges; driver tips of ≈ ₹500–1,000 a trip; and GST. The ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee is collected once by your first hotel and covers 30 days. Ask whether your quote lists each of these, because the cheapest headline price often leaves two or three out.

Watch for three red flags in a very cheap quote: no vehicle model named, lodges described only as 'deluxe' with no name, and a 2-night Lachen and Lachung loop priced below the Lachung-only rate. Each usually means a crowded shared vehicle, a basic room sold as standard, or extras collected in cash up north.

sections.heading: Full trips from Bagdogra or NJP
paras: Most people do not buy North Sikkim on its own. They fly into Bagdogra or take a train to New Jalpaiguri, spend a night or two in Gangtok, and go north from there. The Bagdogra to Gangtok leg is ≈ 124 km and 4.5–5 hours, and a reserved small car costs ≈ ₹3,500–4,500 one way; a shared jeep seat from Siliguri is ≈ ₹400–600. NH10 closes in the monsoon after slides, and then cars run via Kalimpong or Lava, adding an hour or two.
These are our own from-prices for whole trips in 2026, per person on twin sharing, so you can see how the North leg sits inside a holiday.
list: Budget, 3 nights Gangtok and Lachung on shared seats: from ≈ ₹8,500.
Budget, 6 nights Gangtok, Lachen and Lachung with budget hotels: from ≈ ₹18,500.
Value, 5 nights Gangtok and North Sikkim in a private car with 3-star hotels: from ≈ ₹25,000.
Comfort, 6 nights with Dzongu, Lachen and Lachung in a private SUV: from ≈ ₹46,000.
Premium, 6 nights with a top Gangtok hotel and the best Lachung resort: from ≈ ₹1,05,000.

sections.heading: Seasons that move the price
paras: March and late November are the best value: lodges sit near their base rates and the skies are usually good. April to June and October to early December cost 20 to 40 percent more for lodges and 10 to 20 percent more for vehicles, because these are the rhododendron and clear-sky seasons and Indian school and Puja holidays fall in them. Late December spikes again.

January and February are cheap, but snow can close Zero Point and the road above Thangu. July to September is cheapest on paper, but landslides can suspend permits at a day's notice, and the Lachen road was shut for most of 2024 and 2025. A cheap monsoon quote is only cheap if the trip runs.

sections.heading: How to cut the cost safely
paras: The best saving is a full vehicle: four to six people in one SUV. The second is timing: March or the second half of November. The third is choosing standard lodges, because you spend little waking time in them.

Do not save by cutting a night if you are going to Gurudongmar with elders. A third night, ideally a second one in Lachen, gives the body time before 5,183 m and costs ≈ ₹5,000–8,000 more for the whole vehicle. Do not save by skipping travel insurance either: a policy with high-altitude and trip-disruption cover is worth its price on these roads. And always ask, in writing, what is refunded if permits stop before you leave Gangtok.

faqs.q: How much does a 2N/3D North Sikkim package cost?
faqs.a: From Gangtok, a 2N/3D Lachung and Yumthang trip costs about ₹6,500–8,000 per person on a shared seat with a basic lodge and meals. A couple in a reserved Scorpio with standard lodges pays about ₹12,000–14,000 each. Adding Lachen and Gurudongmar adds about ₹1,000–3,000 per person. These are indicative 2026 figures before GST.

faqs.q: How much does a 3N/4D North Sikkim trip cost?
faqs.a: A 3N/4D loop with two nights in Lachen and one in Lachung costs about ₹16,500–17,500 per person for a couple in a reserved SUV with standard lodges and Zero Point. Six friends sharing one vehicle pay about ₹9,500–10,000 each. Shared-seat versions of this loop are rare. Figures are indicative for 2026 and exclude GST.

faqs.q: Is a shared North Sikkim tour safe?
faqs.a: Yes, shared tours use the same registered vehicles, drivers and permits as private ones. The trade-offs are comfort and control: you share the vehicle with strangers, the timetable is fixed and the back bench is cramped on a 5 to 7 hour drive. For families with seniors or children, or anyone prone to car sickness, a reserved vehicle is kinder.

faqs.q: Why is Zero Point charged extra?
faqs.a: Zero Point (Yumesamdong) is 23 km beyond Yumthang on a rough road that is often iced or closed. Drivers charge it as a separate extension, usually ≈ ₹3,000–4,000 per vehicle, decided in Lachung on the morning itself. If cloud or ice is heavy, you can skip it and keep the money. Ask whether your quote includes it.

faqs.q: What vehicle is used for North Sikkim?
faqs.a: Registered North Sikkim SUVs: Bolero and Sumo for most shared seats, Scorpio and Xylo for typical private trips, and Innova or Innova Crysta for more comfort. All carry the same permit. A Crysta costs roughly ₹3,000–5,000 more for a 2-night trip and is worth it with seniors on long drive days.

faqs.q: Are meals included in North Sikkim packages?
faqs.a: Usually dinner and breakfast are included at the Lachung and Lachen lodges, and many packages add lunch on the excursion day. Food is simple: rice, dal, vegetables, egg or chicken, and often noodles or momos. Ask whether lunch on the drive days from Gangtok is included; if not, budget ≈ ₹200–400 a person at roadside stops.

faqs.q: Is GST added to North Sikkim package prices?
faqs.a: Package quotes from registered operators normally attract 5 percent GST, which some show separately and some fold in. A ₹30,000 couple's quote can rise by ₹1,500 if GST is added at the end. Ask for a total that includes GST, the ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee and any Zero Point charge, so you can compare quotes fairly.

faqs.q: Which month is cheapest for North Sikkim?
faqs.a: March and the second half of November give the best value with reliable weather. January and February are cheaper still, but snow can close Zero Point and the Gurudongmar road. July to September is lowest on paper, but landslides can stop permits without warning. Durga Puja week in October and late December are the most expensive.

faqs.q: Do groups save money on North Sikkim trips?
faqs.a: Yes, a lot. Because one vehicle costs the same for two people as for six, a group of six on a 3N/4D loop pays roughly ₹9,500–10,000 each against ₹16,500–17,500 each for a couple, on the same lodges. If you are three, ask us about pairing with another small group on the same dates.
